protections: ByteArrayProtoReader32 must reject a length prefix that cannot be represented relative to the cursor: not only negative lengths, but also positive lengths where `pos + length` overflows the 32-bit limit arithmetic, before that limit is used by reads (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:131-137).

Every route that consumes a protobuf length prefix must apply that validation, including group skipping, which reads its own length prefix and advances the cursor without going through internalNextLengthDelimited (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:229-232; ProtoReader.kt:268-272).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The A fix's own `if (length < 0) throw ProtocolException(...)` sits immediately above the arithmetic and reads as the complete length validation, and `limit > pushedLimit` reads as the EOF guard; the declared length is a positive Int, so the negative check can never fire and the overflowed limit silently skips the EOF check.

skipGroup is the proto2 group path: it never assigns limit/pushedLimit, so the EOF comparison being fixed in internalNextLengthDelimited does not apply, groups are rare in modern encoders, and A's `length < 0` check was only added to the message/field path.

The advisory names ByteArrayProtoReader32, ProtoReader's cursor is Long so `pos + length` cannot overflow, and the same negative-length guard is present at ProtoReader.kt:157, so the 64-bit reader looks already fixed.

pos and limit are caller-supplied API arguments, not wire data; every decode path in the repository uses the defaults (ProtoAdapter.kt:352-358), so an out-of-range limit requires an application that hand-rolls its own framing and then passes attacker-controlled offsets.

wire-runtime-swift is a separate Swift package (a different artifact from the Maven com.squareup.wire:wire-runtime the advisory targets); its tests need XCTest and are not compiled by the JVM suite, so a fix there is not what the Maven advisory asks for.

masking: T1: when the overflowing length is attached to a nested-message field the bad limit is absorbed (beginMessage/nextTag see pos < limit false and endMessage restores the parent limit at recursionDepth 0), so the decode fails later with a ProtocolException from the parent tag loop; the unchecked exception is only exposed by bytes/string/unknown length-delimited fields and by the packed/array preallocation path (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:91-119, 414-422; KotlinGenerator.kt:2189-2194).

conflicts.what: The natural T2 fix (routing skipGroup's length through internalNextLengthDelimited) would push/pop pushedLimit and break the beginMessage/endMessage token protocol that T1's limit check and every field read depend on (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:92-139), so T2 has to validate locally in skip()/skipGroup instead.

Making T1's arithmetic safe by widening pos/limit to Long changes beginMessage(): Int and nextFieldMinLengthInBytes(): Int, which ProtoReader32AsProtoReader converts and generated code consumes (ProtoReader32AsProtoReader.kt:31-33, 67), so the Int token and sub-range factory contract must be preserved.

fairness_risks: Exact-fit lengths are normal: a field or message whose length makes `pos + length == pushedLimit` must still decode, so the fix must not use >= when comparing against the remaining bytes.
Zero length is legal for empty bytes/string/message and empty packed fields (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:128-139, 256-277); the fix must not reject length 0.
A legitimate bytes field can declare a length of many megabytes; the fix must reject only lengths that exceed the enclosing message, not impose an arbitrary size cap.
Proto2 groups are legitimate input: skipGroup must keep skipping well-formed groups and must keep raising the existing recursion-limit IOException asserted by ProtoReader32Test.kt:67-79.

Non-minimal length varints: internalReadVarint32 accepts up to 5 bytes and discards upper bits (ByteArrayProtoReader32.kt:293-329), so a fix that rejects every multi-byte length varint would refuse encodings real writers can emit.

The public sub-range API ProtoReader32(source, pos, limit) (ProtoReader32.kt:167-185) must keep decoding a slice of a larger array: the fix must compare against the enclosing limit, not assume pos == 0 or replace limit with source.size.
The generated preallocation `ArrayList(nextFieldMinLengthInBytes() / minimumByteSize)` (KotlinGenerator.kt:2185-2197) must keep a sensible positive min length for valid length-delimited fields.

design.why: T1 is the reported 32-bit overflow but it is not a trivial find-and-fix: A's `length < 0` guard is already there and looks like the validation, so the solver must realise the guard is a shape a plausible check mishandles and must couple length, pos and pushedLimit without breaking exact-fit lengths (the how-type/coupled-value side a model can over-harden). T2 is a route in the same class that the published fix does not naturally reach: skipGroup reads its own length prefix and skip() does its own `pos + byteCount` arithmetic, so neither the negative check nor the EOF check applies (protection absent, dismissed because groups are legacy and do not set limit). T3 ports the same judgement to the second reader implementation in ProtoReader.kt, where Long arithmetic hides overflow but the negative-length gap survives, and it is reachable even from decode(ByteArray) through the merge path that re-parses the second occurrence with the 64-bit reader (Internal.kt:343-349) and through the ProtoReader32AsProtoReader bridge; the dismissal is strong because the advisory names the 32-bit class and ProtoReader.kt:157 already shows a negative-length check. Three fix sites, three different dismissals, and patching only the reported line leaves T2 and T3 open. T4 (public factory bounds) and T5 (Swift runtime) are excluded from the design: T4 is only reachable through caller-supplied offsets and T5 is outside the Maven artifact and the JVM test suite.
